items.speaker: Constable II
items.text: Move! Constables on duty. Make way!
The sun sets in the west. Meanwhile, constables armed with bows and blades march through the streets.
Like a long, cobalt dragon, they pass by as people watch curiously and whisper to each other, wondering at their destination.
Two constables hurry to reach the young man leading the grim-faced parade.

items.speaker: Yang Wu
items.text: Chief, there's no trace of that reed girl anywhere. She's disappeared.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: I see. Stay sharp and keep an eye out for her. We can't allow any more Yao to escape.

items.speaker: Du Liu
items.text: News from the west gate: two more Yao have been captured. Do you want to question them yourself like last time?

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: I'll be there shortly.

items.speaker: Yang Wu
items.text: We've been walking for a while now. Where are you leading us?
Yáng Wǔ still wants to speak, but their chief raises his right hand, signaling the marching constables behind to stop.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: This is it!
The house before them lies at the street's end. Its doors are tightly shut, but chanting voices escape out through the cracks.
Withered grass devours bone. On icy plain the spirits moan. When the city falls, the Immortal descends. Longevity granted, no death, no end.
All returns to origin. Longevity draws near. Stars will shift only when the true path appears. Depart from this strange world, and find peace in the immortal realm.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Hmph. The source was right. Yao are gathering here.
Chéng Héguāng clenches his fist toward the door, then lifts it in a sharp upward motion.
The metal bolt falls with a clang.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Move in!
He draws his blade and throws the door open. The constables pour into the small square courtyard, ringing their Reversion Bells.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Patrol constables! Civilians, stay back!

items.speaker: Prominent Local Merchant I
items.text: By whose order are you here? Who gave you the right?

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Hmph, quite the posture for a wanted suspect.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: You're all under arrest. Seize them!

items.speaker: Prominent Local Merchant II
items.text: This is outrageous! You jumped-up toll collector! How dare you lay your hands on us!

items.speaker: Prominent Local Merchant II
items.text: Urgh! What on earth is that noise?

items.speaker: Prominent Local Merchant I
items.text: That's enough! I said enough! Stop!
The bells ring under the eaves. Those inside cover their ears, but no tails grow, and no bark forms to cover their skin.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: They're not Yao?
The young chief constable is struck still, grappling with the unexpected outcome. These people dressed in fine silks are wealthy merchants, not Yao cultists.
From outside, older, wiser constables peek in, while the newer, oblivious recruits continue to ring their bells as ordered.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Stop the bells!
The constables stop, and Chéng Héguāng looks over the crowd before sheathing his blade.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: I am Chief Constable Chéng, acting under orders to investigate the Yao involved in the Stilted Parade. I have been instructed to bring them to justice without delay.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: The verses you were reciting are identical to those the Yao chanted at the parade. If I am mistaken, I humbly ask for your forgiveness in advance.

items.speaker: Prominent Local Merchant II
items.text: Can you believe this petulant boy? He thought we were Yao gathering for some evil ritual!

items.speaker: Prominent Local Merchant II
items.text: Watch yourself, "Chief Constable." Slandering a respected merchant like myself could get you in serious trouble!

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: All are equal before the law. I only act in accordance with it. I ask your presence at the Yamen, so please, gentlemen, come with us.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Should you be proven innocent, I will offer my deepest apologies.

items.speaker: Prominent Local Merchant III
items.text: Do you know who you're speaking to, boy?

items.speaker: Prominent Local Merchant III
items.text: I won't leave this house unless your superior comes and explains everything in person!
The air feels heavy as lead. The constables look at each other, no one daring to speak.
For a moment, the standstill feels as if it might go on forever, until the tension is at last cut by a voice from outside.

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: Gentlemen, I'm afraid there's been a misunderstanding.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Sir?
The constables part respectfully as Lì Huìfēng marches into the courtyard, followed by a plump middle-aged man in brocade.

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: Those honorable gentlemen are simply studying the classics and cultivating their minds.

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: It has nothing to do with the turmoil on the streets, nor with the Yao's evil deeds.

items.speaker: Prominent Local Merchant IV
items.text: You speak the truth, Commander. These classics the gentlemen were reciting are scriptures transcribed by His Eminence Zhāng himself! They serve only to enlighten the mind.

items.speaker: Prominent Local Merchant IV
items.text: But no doubt our young Chief Constable here only intended to perform his duties and perhaps leaped to judgment. Is that so, Commander?

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: I thank you for your understanding and your timely message, else this could have been an even greater humiliation. Héguāng, apologize to the honorable gentlemen.
Chéng Héguāng remains silent and stares at the scripture scroll in the man's hand.

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: Chéng Héguāng! Do you not hear me?

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: I acted thoughtlessly. For that I am sorry, Your Excellencies.

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: Do you think that an acceptable apology? When we return to the Yamen, you'll suffer sixty strokes for your insolence!

items.speaker: Prominent Local Merchant IV
items.text: Please, no need to be so harsh, Commander. I'm certain the chief acted with the best intentions. Young men often rush to judgment. We've all done the same.
Speaking back and forth, Lì Huìfēng and the middle-aged merchant ease the tension at last.
A look passes among those in the courtyard. The obvious leader among them speaks.

items.speaker: Prominent Local Merchant I
items.text: No real harm has been done to us; do not punish him for doing his duty.

items.speaker: Prominent Local Merchant II
items.text: Just be sure to keep your officers in line, Lì!

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: Of course. Your generosity is greatly appreciated, gentlemen. We shall take our leave.
Lì Huìfēng says no more and signals for the constables to leave the courtyard.
A wounded cobalt dragon retreats back to its cave in the form of a slow and dreary procession of downcast faces.
Lì Huìfēng stands ahead, unconcerned with the sour faces of the lower ranks behind him.
With their commander present, the constables dare not even speak as they pass through the doors of the Yamen and file away to the mess hall.
Only Chéng Héguāng remains by the entrance, struggling to hold his head high. The result is something stiff and strange but proud.

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: Why are you standing there like a statue? It's time to eat.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: I'm awaiting my sixty strokes.
Lì Huìfēng puts down the case file and looks at him with a complex expression.

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: *sigh* There won't be any coming. Now, go eat.
But he still does not move.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: If you've elected to spare me, then allow me a question, Commander.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: The man who came with you had a scroll in his hand. Where did it come from? There's a Bagua array on it, formed by a Mei tree and a jade sword.

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: Héguāng, if I spare you the punishment, you ought to at least do me the courtesy of sparing me the questions.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Then I would rather take the punishment.
The evening wind blows through the hall, and the candlelight flickers in response.

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: Do you really have no inkling of who you offended tonight?

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: I do not.

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: The Chén family, respected gentry with three Imperial Scholars in only a few decades. Lord Lù, a corps leader, his family have served in the military for generations. And the Lǐs—I needn't remind you who they are.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: I am but the son of bandits. I don't know any of these high lords.

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: Now you know.
Lì Huìfēng looks away and reads from the case file.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: The man with the scroll—is he of noble birth, too?
He does not receive an answer.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Am I right to assume that you've kept me from investigating the School of Mei, not because you feared I might alarm them, but because you are aware of the school's prestigious background?
The words are pointed but do not break his commander's grim silence.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: You know they're responsible for the turmoil in the county, yet you permit these men to walk free, allowing the common Yao to take the fall—

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: Enough!
Lì Huìfēng rises with an expression as fiery as a lit rocket as he throws the files to the ground.

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: Are you so naive? Do you truly have no clue as to why you were spared today?

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Because of your connection to the man with the scroll.

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: Then you do have some inkling of what's going on!

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: You did well capturing those Yao, and I had planned to speak highly of you before Lord Lù. But after your actions today—storming into a civilian's home, attempting to arrest all present—how can I possibly recommend you!?

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: Have you forsaken your vow and decided to live in your father's disgrace forever?

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: I would never!
He grits his teeth but does not give an inch.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: But Commander, this is more important than my name. This is for the safety of the townspeople!

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: Alright. Then tell me exactly what harm the School of Mei has done and what crime you accuse them of.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: As my prior report states, they are practicing sorcery and other forbidden arts.

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: They fabricated the descent of a deity at the parade, yes. But have you caught any of the offenders from that day?

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Not yet.

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: And has any member of the school actually committed a crime? Or have you found some scripture that proves their evil intention?

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: I have not.

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: So you have nothing. You wish me to convince the magistrate to act against the School of Mei, risking the anger of officials and high lords based on nothing? Hm?

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: The school will claim that they were only teaching the methods to strengthen the body and enrich the mind, and that the Yao were foolish and greedy to think their practices could grant longevity.

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: We cannot act on hearsay and rumors, especially when it may anger the high lords!

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: You're right. I lack the evidence to refute your words.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: But if it is the lords that worry you, I will investigate in secret. Three days is all I need. I will find the proof.

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: Enough.
Another cold blast of wind sweeps through the hall, rustling the papers on his desk.
Lì Huìfēng uses a paperweight to smooth the files and sits back into his chair.

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: Go now. Get some rest.

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: Your men are to be placed under the captain, Zhāng; he knows the county well. You will remain, but only as his backup.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Why? I've done nothing wrong!

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: *sigh* Then you've not listened to a word I've said.
The water in the pot boils, the lid rattles, the steam whistles, and Lì Huìfēng pays it no attention.
Steam fills Chéng Héguāng's sight.
The pot at last boils over.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Commander!

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Must the people's blood be spilled before we act?

items.speaker: Li Huifeng
items.text: Watch your tongue!
In the tea bowl on the desk, weak ripples form.
The young man stands solid, silent for a long time, rooted like a tree as the steam fades from him.
At last, he breaks the roots and turns.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Perhaps I have not listened, Commander.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Goodnight.
Cheng's House, Ancient Zhu County
The cool moon shines like a lantern over a dark lake.
Chéng Héguāng puts down a book and rubs his tired neck.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: *sigh* It's getting late.
He lights a blackened torch with a candle, holding the light as he steps into the dark.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Zhòngní said, "One of virtue follows the course of the Mean; one of cunning turns from it."

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: "Following the Mean, the virtuous acts in due measure. Turning from the Mean, the cunning moves without restraint."
He stops at the door, deep in thought.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Fortunately, it's still not too late.
A street cat cries out nearby.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Hm? That's ...

items.speaker: Night Watch
items.text: Fire! Fire!
A man runs in panic. Behind him, plumes of smoke leap and billow into the sky.

items.speaker: Night Watch
items.text: There's a fire at Chief Constable Chéng's house!
